title: NEXORA verification matrix
description: Every claim this repository makes that nothing checks, as data. The corpus labels such a claim `Verified: NO — deferred to Phase 2` at the point of use -- ADR-0001 rule 9 and `docs/adr/README.md` make the label mandatory, and `docs/architecture/20-target-repository-layout.md` §13 makes this document the owner of every one of them. A label scattered through 44 documents is not a queue; it is a rumour. This file is the queue: one row per obligation, each row naming what is unverified, why it is not already checkable, who can close it, and the concrete artefact that closes it -- an existing `LIVE-NN` row, a CI step, an assertion in `packages/schema/scripts/verify.mjs`, a tool, a decision recorded in `docs/PROJECT-STATE.md` §9, or a browser measurement this host cannot take. The rows are anchored, not summarised: every row lists `at` entries of `{doc, anchor}`, where `anchor` is a verbatim fragment of the line carrying the label, and `scripts/verify.mjs` re-derives the label inventory from `docs/**` on every run and refuses three failures the prose cannot see -- a labelled claim no row answers, an anchor that no longer points at a labelled line, and a line counted twice. The corpus vocabulary (the sentences that *define* the label rather than carry a claim) is listed separately for the same reason. `docs/verification/live-matrix.md` is not re-typed here: its 24 rows are inherited by id and its `Verified:` column is read from it on every run, because a second copy of 24 rows is a second thing that can be wrong. `docs/architecture/39-verification-matrix.md` is the argument; this is the list.

marker.why: Two vocabularies are in use across the corpus -- `Verified: NO — deferred to Phase 2` and the bare `**NO — Phase 2**` of the table columns in docs/architecture/35-38 -- and both are deferred claims. They are one alternation so that `Verified: NO — deferred to Phase 2` counts once, not twice. The leading `\b` is load-bearing: without it, `UNVERIFIED: no lockfile is tracked` reads as a `Verified: NO` claim and the queue inherits a row nobody wrote.
marker.where: docs/**/*.md, excluding docs/architecture/39-verification-matrix.md itself -- this document is the queue, not a claim in it

meaning.no-code: the thing the claim is about does not exist yet -- no Connector, no compiler, no UI screen. Nothing can assert it until Phase 2 writes the component.
meaning.no-check: the thing exists (a contract, a document rule, an inherited file) and nothing asserts the claim about it. Closing it is a checker, not a feature.
meaning.no-run: a check exists and is green where it has run, but it has not run where the claim needs it -- an executed ladder, a live row, a real browser.
meaning.no-fixture: the assertion is writable today but the input that would make it mean something (an ambiguous-format feed, a v4 envelope, a second sync backend) is not in `packages/schema/examples/` or `fixtures/`.
meaning.needs-human: the row cannot be closed by code: a decision from docs/PROJECT-STATE.md §9, a value only a browser can measure, or a store-side behaviour nobody in this repository controls.

states.why: The five states are five different jobs. A queue that only said 'not verified' would put 'write the Go compiler' and 'add one invalid example file' in the same column, and the first reading of it would be a wall.

meaning.connector: Go code under `connector/` plus its tests -- the supervisor, compiler, keystore, prober.
meaning.extension: the browser side: `nexora/extension/**` and the inherited `omega-*` behaviour it must not break.
meaning.packages: `packages/protocol`, `packages/state`, `packages/i18n` -- the TypeScript layer between UI and contract.
meaning.ui: a claim only reviewable per screen, which no automated check can close (constraint 11).
meaning.contracts: `packages/schema`: a field, an error code, a fixture or an assertion in `scripts/verify.mjs`.
meaning.tools: a Node script under `tools/` that fails the build.
meaning.ci: `.github/workflows/verify.yml` -- a step that runs on every push.
meaning.human: docs/PROJECT-STATE.md §9: the row is a question, and the check comes after the answer.
meaning.external: a browser, an OS, or a store: measurable only by a run this repository does not own.

meaning.live-row: closed by executing an existing `LIVE-NN` row of docs/verification/live-matrix.md; `ref` is that id.
meaning.new-live-row: closed by a `LIVE-NN` row that does not exist yet and must be written first -- the honest version of 'there is a test for it'.
meaning.assertion: closed by a named assertion: a `check()` in packages/schema/scripts/verify.mjs, or the named test of a Phase-2 suite (a golden config, a registry load test, a client codec test). `ref` is the label or test name that will print when it runs, and the harness requires it to be absent today.
meaning.gate: closed by a guard in the repository (import graph, path set, manifest diff).
meaning.tool: closed by a Node script under tools/, named by its path.
meaning.decision: closed by an answer to docs/PROJECT-STATE.md §9; the check follows the answer.
meaning.external-measurement: closed by a measurement in a browser or on a store, recorded with its date and cohort.

closingKinds.why: A row whose closing mechanism is 'Phase 2' is a wish. Every row here names an artefact that can be missing or present, which is what makes the queue auditable against the Phase-2 diff.

live.inherited: the 24 `LIVE-NN` rows are the live half of this matrix; they are not re-typed here, and this file is wrong the day their ids stop matching.
live.statusColumn: read from the source on every run: `NO — Phase 2` means specified but unexecuted, `PARTIAL` means a Phase-1 artefact checks part of it, and nothing is ever `YES` in this iteration.
live.promotion: docs/verification/live-matrix.md §'Promotion rules' rule 2 makes `LIVE-04` (egress proof) a precondition of `LIVE-05…LIVE-09`; that rule is why nine transport rows below inherit from one row rather than claiming independence.
live.rule: A row here that closes by `live-row` inherits that row's status. When a live row is executed, the rows pointing at it move from `no-run` to green in the same commit; a design document may not report a live row as done on the strength of its specification.

retired.rule: A row closes by deletion -- §9 rule 2 of docs/architecture/39-verification-matrix.md forbids closing it by editing its state -- and the id it held retires here. Ids are never renumbered or recycled: that is ADR-0001 rule 2 for ADR numbers, and the queue takes it because a `VER-NN` is cited across the corpus, in the step names of .github/workflows/verify.yml, and verbatim in runner logs, so renumbering would silently change what every earlier citation means. The harness refuses an id that is both live and retired, a retired id that is not in the issued range, and any hole in that range this list does not name -- which is what keeps a deletion a declared closure rather than a disappearance.

matrix.why: `connector/cmd/nexora-connector/config_apply.go` is the whole of doc 27 §2 and §8 in one `Handle`: compare-and-swap against the applied-state record, read the intent, compile, write atomically, reserve the ports, stop and start Core -- and `config_apply_test.go` refuses each of those steps in turn to show nothing after it moved. The half that does not exist is who calls it. `connector/cmd/nexora-connector/main.go` registers `connector.hello` and `connector.version` and nothing else, so a real frame for this method answers `UnknownMethod` at the dispatch door; and the surface's one input seam -- an intent source that turns `profileIds` into the profiles, servers, routing, settings and failure policy stage 1 resolves -- is satisfied only by a test double that returns what the test put in it. That is not a missing file the design could fill in: `packages/schema/protocol/commands/config.apply.json#/args` is `additionalProperties: false` over ids, while the `intent-down` entry of `packages/schema/protocol/data-ownership.json#/movements` says the payload of this very command is 'intent documents: profiles, servers, routing, settings -- references, never values' from the browser plane, where every one of those stores lives (`docs/architecture/34-data-split.md` §6). Whichever way the documents arrive, the same row then needs the two directories the surface is constructed with -- no contract names the state directory or the compiled-config directory, and `compiled-config.location` ('name derived from the config hash') disagrees with `connector/internal/apply`'s one stable file name, which is the shape doc 27 §8's rename depends on. The test seam chose all three; `ODEC-39` is the register saying which choices are the contract's.

matrix.subject: the format an `auto` parse resolves to has nowhere to be recorded: doc 29 §5 promises `auto` never survives into a stored source, and no artefact in the contract carries the detector that won

at.anchor: records which detector won

matrix.why: `docs/architecture/29-subscriptions-and-servers.md` §5 makes two claims about one enum value: `auto` is legal only while exactly one parser's detector answers true, and it is 'meant never to survive into a stored source' because the parser records which one won. The second claim has no home anywhere in the corpus. `packages/schema/protocol/commands/subscription.refresh.json#/result` bounds a `refreshed[]` item with `additionalProperties: false` over eight properties -- `subscriptionId`, `sha256`, `serverCount`, `added`, `removed`, `duplicates`, `lossyFields`, `servers` -- none of them a format, and the same file's `#/args` states the opposite duty in its own words: the Connector 'writes none of them back -- the result is not a mutated source'. Detection belongs to the Connector (doc 29 §2), the source document belongs to the extension (`docs/architecture/34-data-split.md` §6), and the one channel between those planes is the eight fields above. So either the result gains a field and the extension persists what the parser chose, or §5's sentence is wrong about the storage and `auto` does survive, in which case an ambiguous body fails once per refresh rather than once per source and the document should say that instead. Both readings are a field and a sentence in `packages/schema`, which is why this is `contract` and why the row waits on `ODEC-40` rather than on a parser.

matrix.subject: the pipe half of the version negotiation has no artefact to be written down in: `docs/architecture/21-system-context.md` §6 promises the negotiation result reaches the connector log and `diagnostics.get`, and every field that could carry it names only the browser-side number

at.anchor: negotiated versions reach the connector log

matrix.why: `docs/architecture/21-system-context.md` §6 ends the case for two processes with a consequence: 'a shim from NEXORA 3.7 may legally talk to a connector from 3.6 when both sides' declared floors overlap, so the negotiation result must be *written down* in the connector log and surfaced in `diagnostics.get`'. The overlap it is describing is the pipe's, not the browser's -- the two processes are joined by the pipe, and §6 is the paragraph about why they are separate -- and since 2026-11-06 the contract says there are two independent windows: `packages/schema/protocol/framing.json#/versionFloors` declares four numbers over `protocol` (`protocolVersion`, `minCompatibleProtocolVersion`, 'negotiatedIn: connector.hello') and `pipe` (`frameFormatVersion`, `minPipeVersion`, 'negotiatedIn: the v field of every frame'), and `packages/schema/protocol/error-taxonomy.json#/codes` refuses both with the single `VersionMismatch` whose own `meaning` says 'today the window that is negotiated is the protocol one'. Nothing in this repository's vocabulary can say the other half. `connector.connected` is the event `packages/schema/observability.json#/events` nominates as the thing that 'writes it down', and its payload is `additionalProperties: false` over exactly `protocolVersion`, `capabilities` and `adoptedExisting`; the `versions` entry of `#/diagnosticsSections` contains 'extension version, Connector version, Core version, protocolVersion, negotiated capabilities'; `#/export/footer/fields` names `protocolVersion` once among ten. The command could in principle answer more: `packages/schema/protocol/commands/diagnostics.get.json#/result` is closed over five properties and its `payload` is `type: ['object', 'null']` with no shape at all, so a section body is the one place an undeclared number could sit and the one place nothing bounds it. The runtime reaches nowhere near either: `connector/internal/hello`'s `Session` holds the negotiation as an unexported `agreed *Answer` and hands the front door only `Negotiated` and `Capabilities`, and `connector/internal/envelope` range-checks an inbound frame's `v` against the envelope's 1..255 and never against `MinPipeVersion`. That the number is not compared is stated plainly in `docs/architecture/25-native-messaging-protocol.md` §1 and in `VER-18`'s tombstone, so this row is not about the missing comparison; it is about the missing name. The other half of the promise -- that no record is written at all, since no file under `connector/**` imports a logging package and nothing emits a `connector.connected` frame -- is doc 36 §16's fifth open item and the runtime rows, which is why this row is `contracts` and not `connector`: the blocker is a field, an enum and two `contains` sentences, and `ODEC-41` is where choosing them belongs.
